claims.text: One document, in the spec's records (decision D-090-1), states Glossa's record system (D1), projection rule (D2), and primitive-absolute disposition (D3) in the skeleton's terms. It is written and frozen before any G2 derivation is attempted, and any later change to it is a new version under a recorded amendment act, so the document the G2 stage and any independent reader cite is identifiable by hash. This does not establish: that the document's definitions are right — only that exactly one citable document carries them, stated before results, as G1 requires.

claims.text: The G1 document defines the record system over the classes the program's verdicts actually rest on — corpus records (the inscription files and their loaders), anchor records (the anchors register), and ledger claim lines — naming for each class what a record is, what provenance it carries, and its population counted from the records at the state read. A record that breaks its class's stated provenance rule is accounted for by the definition (named as an exception class with its count — as the anchors register's 3 `no_validation_record` entries require), never silently absorbed. This does not establish: that the records are complete or correct — only that the system the study reasons about is the system the program actually has, provenance rules and exceptions stated.

claims.text: The G1 document either (a) names exactly one primitive absolute in D3's sense — a quantity taken as given in absolute terms, not relative to the records — with the audit showing every other absolute-looking input to be record-relative or derived from the named one; or (b) proves none is needed, by exhibiting each candidate absolute as record-relative or derived. claims.text: The study closes with an outcome record stating the per-stage outcomes (G1: STATED or NOT YET with the missing element named; G2: DERIVED or NOT YET with the obstruction named) and the study-level outcome as spec.md defines it (INSTANTIATES-path, ANALOGY with the metaphorical element named, or NOT YET with the missing work stated), each with evidence pointers to the stage records. The outcome — or, if a stage cannot run, the blocker — is reported to the VEXA chat for the improvement registry, as the commission requires. The formal verdict over the full G1–G5 bar belongs to the independent reader under the judging protocol; this study does not issue it. This does not establish: that the reported outcome is the final verdict on the domain — the reader's verdict under the protocol, and the G3–G5 follow-on, both stand after it.
